Access · Security · Backup

Reaching and protecting a home server: Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel, vzdump

A home server is only as good as its access and its backups. My principle: no port forwarding, every access path a conscious decision, a backup every day.

Serge Zabolotny · 2026-10-25

  • Tailscale
  • Cloudflare Tunnel
  • Zero Trust
  • vzdump
  • Backup
  • Uptime Kuma
  • Fail2ban
  • Homelab

Who gets access from where?

Who / whatSolution
Only me, privately and on the moveTailscale (WireGuard VPN)
Only me, in the browser without VPNCloudflare Tunnel + Access (login via one-time PIN)
Other peopleTunnel with two-factor login or a strong password
Sensitive data (e.g. photos)Via Tailscale only, never public

The Cloudflare Tunnel makes an outbound connection, so no port has to be opened on the router. How I locked down an exposed dashboard with it is in the note Zero Trust for the homelab.

Everyday protection

  • Fail2ban blocks addresses after repeated failed attempts.
  • AdGuard filters ads and trackers via DNS across the whole network.
  • Uptime Kuma alerts you when a service becomes unreachable; Glances shows the load on the host.
  • Regularly check what DNS and the tunnel actually publish.

Backups with vzdump

Proxmox backs up whole containers with vzdump. Mine runs daily to a separate disk, keeping 7 daily, 4 weekly and 3 monthly backups:

vzdump <CTID> --storage <backup-storage> --mode snapshot \
  --prune-backups keep-daily=7,keep-weekly=4,keep-monthly=3

Important: a second disk in the same machine protects against disk failure, not against theft, fire or power surges. By the 3-2-1 rule at least one copy belongs in another location – and a backup only counts once you have tested the restore.

Checklist

  • No port forwarding on the router
  • A login layer for every public service
  • Private services via VPN only
  • Daily backup to a separate disk, plus a copy in another location
  • Test restores regularly
  • Monitoring with alerts
